thread:
kevin-support: Customer ACME Prod reporting a sudden p99 spike on /v1/generate — baseline ~450ms, now seeing 1.8-2.4s since ~11:03. They started seeing a bunch of timeouts and a few 401s around same time.

kevin-support: stack: ACME->frontend->call to redwood hosted endpoint. They say it correlates with a token rotation on their side. Ticket #CS-7123, attaching logs.

nitya-eng-platform: thanks — can you paste a minimal repro + the tenant id? also which model/route?

kevin-support: tenant=acme-prod, route=/v1/generate, model=gpt-small-quant, example curl:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}'
```

kevin-support: logs show repeated short requests (50-200 tokens) with many tiny retry bursts after 401s.

matt-eng-sre: this smells like continuous-batcher hold/grace + many tiny arrivals causing head-of-line latency. tiny bursts + auth retries -> many microbatches that trigger long KV-cache/initialization cost. can we see their batcher config?

kevin-support: they are on default tenant overrides. I fetched the runtime config from our console:
```
continuous_batcher:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 32
  grace_window_ms: 12
  batch_timeout_ms: 28
  min_batch_fill: 1
```

kevin-support: they also have short-lived tokens (client rotates every ~60s) per billing-bot note.

billing-bot: FYI ACME had an automated KMS rotation and their SDKs rolled tokens aggressively between 10:58-11:10. saw ~7 token refresh events from their account.

nitya-eng-platform: ok that explains frequent auth failures that convert a steady stream into many tiny requests. continuous_batcher params above are tuned for cost, not for pathological tiny bursts. raising batch_timeout or lowering grace window could help depending on pattern.

matt-eng-sre: proposed quick mitigations:
- increase batch_timeout_ms to 80-120 temporarily for tenant acme-prod to allow more coalescing (reduces p99 but slightly increases p95 for warm flows)
- set min_batch_fill: 2 to avoid serving one-off single-request batches when retries spike
- short-term: route tenant to a small dedicated pool (reserved) to avoid noisy neighbors while we stabilize

nitya-eng-platform: commands to patch via control plane:
```
redwoodctl rollout patch --tenant acme-prod \\
  --set continuous_batcher.batch_timeout_ms=100 \\
  --set continuous_batcher.min_batch_fill=2
```

nitya-eng-platform: I'll stage the patch in canary for 2 instances, monitor p50/p95/p99 for 10min, then roll.

sara-oncall: add a metrics breakpoint: alert if p99 > 1s for 5m and error rate > 1% so we don't cause churn. also capture trace for a sample request id.

matt-eng-sre: quick repro steps for local:
1) run a script to issue many short requests with an intermittent 401 injected (simulate token rotation).
2) measure p99 with batcher settings above.
sample script snippet:
```
# loop that sometimes sends invalid token
for i in seq 1 1000; do
  if (( i % 37 == 0 )); then head -c 16 /dev/urandom | base64 | xargs -I{} curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer invalid{}" ... &
  else
    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $VALID" ... &
  fi
  sleep 0.005
done
```

kevin-support: ACME gives permission to apply tenant-scoped patch. please proceed.

nitya-eng-platform: applying canary patch now to 2 hosts. will watch metrics.

oncall-bot: [incident] patch-deploy started by nitya-eng-platform at 2024-06-12T15:22:30Z (canary=2/2).

nitya-eng-platform: canary looks promising — p99 dropped from ~1.9s -> ~420ms on canary nodes, p95 slightly up ~50ms.

matt-eng-sre: good. roll to full cluster but keep min_batch_fill=2. also schedule follow-up to investigate SDK token refresh pattern; ideally clients should backoff and avoid immediate retries on 401.

sara-oncall: assigned follow-up: nitya-eng-platform (apply change), matt-eng-sre (repro + perf test), kevin-support (coordinate ACME). target: full rollout in 30m if metrics stable.

kevin-support: ACME confirmed improved UX after canary. will keep ticket open for token rotation fix on their side. :thumbsup:

matt-eng-sre: long-term notes for product: consider tenant-level autoset that increases batch_timeout when many tiny requests detected or when auth-failure-rate spikes — adaptive coalescing. file a PR for design doc.

oncall-bot: [incident] patch-deploy completed at 2024-06-12T15:45:12Z (success).

sara-oncall: closing loop here. update CS ticket and add mitigation steps to runbook under "continuous-batcher / auth-induced tiny bursts".

kevin-support: thanks everyone, ACME very happy. closing thread.
